terminal.intro: The terminal is a window where you type text commands to your computer, with no menus or buttons.

bloques.cuerpo: You type a command, press Enter, and the machine runs it instantly. Each command is a verb: `ls` lists, `cd` enters a folder, `mkdir` creates one.
To create a folder and step into it: `mkdir my-project` then `cd my-project`. Two lines do what would take several clicks with a mouse.
Almost every dev tool (Git, Node, npm) lives in the terminal. Getting comfortable here makes you much faster and is the first step to everything else.

git.intro: Git records the history of your code: every change is saved, so you can go back whenever you need to.

bloques.cuerpo: You work and, when something works, you make a `commit`: a snapshot of your project at that moment with a message explaining what changed.
If you break something today, you can return to yesterday's commit without losing a thing. With `branches` you try new ideas without touching the version that already works.
It's how teams work on the same project without stepping on each other. Without Git, real collaboration is impossible.

htmlcss.intro: HTML lays the bricks of a page; CSS paints and arranges them. Together they're the foundation of everything you see on the web.

bloques.cuerpo: HTML describes content with tags (`<h1>` for a heading, `<button>` for a button). CSS decides how it looks: color, size, position.
`<button>Send</button>` creates the button; in CSS, `button { background: blue; border-radius: 8px; }` makes it blue with rounded corners.
No interface exists without HTML and CSS. React, Next.js and Tailwind build on top of this, so knowing it well saves you pain later.

javascript.intro: JavaScript brings the web to life: it makes pages react to what the user does.

bloques.cuerpo: With JS you respond to events (a click, a keypress), change the page on the fly, and fetch data from a server without reloading.
A button that shows a message on click: `button.addEventListener('click', () => alert('Hi!'))`. HTML draws it, JS makes it respond.
It's the only language that runs natively in the browser and also on the server (Node.js). The entire FWD stack leans on it.

react.intro: React is a library for building interfaces out of reusable pieces called components.

bloques.cuerpo: You split the screen into components (a button, a card, a form) and React updates only what changes when the data changes.
A `<Card title="React" />` component you reuse as many times as you want, each with its own content, without repeating code.
It's the heart of the frontend at FWD Talent. Almost everything you build on the visual side goes through React.

typescript.intro: TypeScript is JavaScript with a safety net: you add types so errors show up before they reach the user.

bloques.cuerpo: You tell each variable what kind of data it holds (text, number, list). If you get it wrong, the editor warns you as you type.
`function greet(name: string)` makes it clear it expects text. Pass it a number and TypeScript flags it before anything runs.
In growing projects, types are living documentation and prevent tricky bugs. The FWD repo is `strict`, so it's part of daily work.

nextjs.intro: Next.js is the React framework FWD uses: it gives you routing, server rendering and deployment ready for production.

bloques.cuerpo: Each file inside the routes folder becomes a page. You can render on the server so it loads fast and looks good to search engines.
Creating `app/projects/page.tsx` automatically gives you the `/projects` route, with nothing else to configure.
It's the base FWD Talent runs on. Learning it brings you straight to how the real product is built.

tailwind.intro: Tailwind lets you design by applying utility classes right in your HTML, without jumping to separate CSS files.

bloques.cuerpo: Instead of writing CSS, you compose styles from small classes: `p-4` adds padding, `rounded-full` rounds corners, `bg-primary` sets the background.
`<button class="px-4 py-2 rounded-full bg-primary">` is a fully styled button, without opening a `.css` file.
It speeds up design a lot and keeps everything consistent with the design tokens. It's the styling standard in the FWD repo.

nodejs.intro: Node.js lets you run JavaScript outside the browser, on the server side. It's your gateway to the backend.

bloques.cuerpo: The same language you use on the frontend now handles requests, reads databases and returns responses from a server.
With a few lines you spin up a server that replies 'Hello' when someone visits an address. That's the building block of any API.
FWD's BackEnd runs on Node. Knowing it lets you work on both sides of the project with a single language.

apis.intro: A REST API is the language the frontend and backend speak: one asks, the other answers.

bloques.cuerpo: The frontend makes a request to an address (`GET /projects`) and the backend returns data, usually as JSON.
`GET /projects` fetches the project list; `POST /projects` creates a new one. Each verb (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) is a different intent.
This is exactly how FWD's FrontEnd and BackEnd talk. Understanding REST is understanding how data flows through the app.

supabase.intro: Supabase is the database and login system FWD uses: Postgres with superpowers, ready to go.

bloques.cuerpo: It gives you a Postgres database, user authentication and file storage, all reachable from your code.
Signing up a user or saving a project are direct calls to Supabase, which handles security with row-level rules (RLS).
It's FWD Talent's data layer. All the progress, profiles and projects live there.

postgres.intro: PostgreSQL is a relational database: it stores information in orderly tables that relate to each other.

bloques.cuerpo: You organize data into tables with columns and rows. Tables relate: a project belongs to a company, an application to a junior.
A `projects` table and a `companies` table connect through an id, so each project knows which company it belongs to without duplicating data.
It's the engine behind Supabase and almost every serious backend. Modeling data well avoids problems that get expensive later.

sql.intro: SQL is the language for asking a database questions and getting back exactly the data you need.

bloques.cuerpo: You write queries that describe what you want: filter, sort, count or join tables. The database returns the result.
`SELECT name FROM projects WHERE status = 'published'` returns just the names of published projects.
Any app that stores data ends up needing SQL. It's a skill that pays off in frontend, backend and data analysis alike.

python.intro: Python is a readable, versatile language, a favorite for data and artificial intelligence.

bloques.cuerpo: Its syntax reads almost like English, which makes it great for quick prototyping and for analyzing information.
`for project in projects: print(project)` walks a list and shows each item. Simple and direct.
It's the gateway to the world of data and AI. With Python you analyze datasets and train models without fighting the language.

ia_fundamentos.intro: AI fundamentals explain how models learn: instead of coding rules, you show them examples and they find patterns.

bloques.cuerpo: A Machine Learning model trains on lots of labeled data and, from there, makes predictions about new data.
Showing it thousands of emails marked 'spam' or 'not spam' until it learns to classify one it has never seen.
Understanding what a model can and can't do lets you bring AI into your products with judgment, no magic and no fear.

ia_prompting.intro: Professional prompting is the craft of asking an AI well to get useful, reliable results.

bloques.cuerpo: A good prompt gives context, states the role, the output format and examples. The clearer you are, the better the model responds.
Instead of 'write about React', ask: 'Explain React to a junior in 3 bullet points, with a code example'. The result changes completely.
It's the skill that multiplies all the others: it lets you use AI as a copilot in any task, from code to design.

sections.title: 1. Introduction and Acceptance
paragraphs: Welcome to the FWD Talent Freelance Projects Marketplace, an initiative of Fundación Forward Costa Rica. This document constitutes a legally binding agreement between you (the "User") and Fundación Forward Costa Rica ("the Foundation"). By using this platform, you fully accept these Terms and Conditions.

sections.title: 2. Nature of the Service
paragraphs: Our platform operates solely as a technological intermediation space. Its purpose is to connect graduates of the Foundation ("FWD Juniors") with companies or clients ("Companies") seeking talent for short-term projects.

sections.title: 3. Registration and Eligibility
paragraphs: To register as a Junior, it is a strict requirement to be a certified graduate of the training programs of Fundación Forward Costa Rica. Companies may register after a commercial validation process. Use of the platform is restricted to adults.

sections.title: 4. User Accounts and Security
paragraphs: The User is solely responsible for safeguarding the confidentiality of their credentials. Sharing accounts, transferring them, or creating fake profiles is strictly prohibited. All activity carried out from an account will be considered the responsibility of its holder.

sections.title: 5. Role of FWD Juniors
paragraphs: Juniors use the platform to access their first paid or pro-bono professional opportunities (as specified in each project), build experience, and expand their portfolio. They must always act with professionalism, honesty, and diligence.

sections.title: 6. Role of Companies
paragraphs: Companies gain access to emerging talent at competitive costs. They commit to providing an environment of respect, clear communication, and constructive feedback, acknowledging that they are working with profiles in a formative or junior stage.

sections.title: 7. Project Publishing Rules
paragraphs: Every project must have clear requirements, defined deadlines, and realistic expectations. The publication of illegal, offensive, or discriminatory projects, or those involving the development of malicious software, is not allowed.

sections.title: 8. Application Rules
paragraphs: Juniors must apply only to projects for which they have the required skills and the necessary time availability. Unjustified abandonment of a project will negatively impact their reputation on the platform.

sections.title: 9. Prohibition of Artificial Intelligence in Applications
sections.note: All communication and cover letters must be of human authorship. The exclusive use of Artificial Intelligence (ChatGPT, Claude, etc.) to generate automated messages is prohibited. We value authenticity over machine-generated syntactic perfection.

sections.title: 10. Selection and Awarding Process
paragraphs: The Company is solely responsible for evaluating and selecting the right candidate. The Foundation offers "matching" tools, but does not guarantee an award, nor does it require the Company to select a specific Junior.

sections.title: 11. Project Development and Execution
paragraphs: Once the project has started, both parties agree to work under agile methodologies or the agreed-upon standards. The Foundation does not supervise or audit the code generated by Juniors or the guidelines of Companies.

sections.title: 12. Communication
paragraphs: Users are encouraged to keep preliminary communication within the platform for security and transparency. The Foundation reserves the right to audit communications within the ecosystem in the event of reported disputes.

sections.title: 13. Payments and Compensation
paragraphs: The platform does not act as a payment processor. Every economic agreement is negotiated, invoiced, and settled externally between the Company and the Junior. The Foundation does not charge transactional commissions for the awarding of projects.

sections.title: 14. Employment Relationship
paragraphs: At no point is an employment relationship (employer-employee) established between the Foundation and the Junior, nor inherently between the Company and the Junior (unless they sign a formal employment contract outside the platform). The default nature of projects is freelance or independent professional services.

sections.title: 15. Intellectual Property of Deliverables
paragraphs: As a general rule, once the agreed payment is settled, the economic rights over the code and the developed product are transferred to the Company. The author's moral rights are inalienable under applicable law.

sections.title: 16. Portfolio Rights
paragraphs: Unless explicitly prohibited via an NDA (Non-Disclosure Agreement), Juniors retain the right to mention the project, describe the architecture, and show screenshots of the public interface in their professional portfolios for the purpose of career promotion.

sections.title: 17. Confidentiality and NDAs
paragraphs: Companies may require the signing of a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) before sharing sensitive details. It is the Junior's responsibility to read, understand, and comply with the restrictions of any legal contract signed externally.

sections.title: 18. Conduct and Code of Conduct
paragraphs: Zero tolerance for harassment, discrimination, extortion, abusive language, or fraudulent practices. Any violation of the code of conduct will result in the immediate expulsion of the offender from the FWD Talent ecosystem.

sections.title: 19. Liability and Limitations (Disclaimer)
paragraphs: The Foundation provides the platform "as is" without implied warranties. We will not be liable for indirect damages, loss of profits, loss of data, or business interruptions arising from the use of the platform or the outcome of freelance projects.

sections.title: 20. Privacy and Data Processing
paragraphs: All collection and processing of personal data is governed by our Privacy Policy, aligned with the relevant national regulations. Information is used exclusively for "matching" purposes and platform operation.

sections.title: 21. Dispute Resolution
paragraphs: Differences between a Company and a Junior must be resolved by mutual agreement. The Foundation does not offer legal mediation or arbitration services and is exempt from participating in any litigation arising from project execution.

sections.title: 22. Changes to the Terms
paragraphs: We reserve the right to modify these Terms at any time. Any update will be notified through the platform. Continued use implies acceptance of the new terms.

sections.title: 1. General Information and Data Controller
paragraphs: At Fundación Forward Costa Rica and the FWD Talent ecosystem, we value and respect your privacy. This Privacy Policy describes how we collect, use, store, share, and protect your personal information when you use our Freelance Projects Marketplace. The data controller is Fundación Forward Costa Rica.

sections.title: 2. Data We Collect
paragraphs: We collect information to provide and improve our services. This includes:
items: Registration data: Name, email, password (encrypted), and role (Junior or Company).
Professional information (FWD Juniors): Technical skills, portfolio links (GitHub, LinkedIn, Behance), educational history at the Foundation, and experience.
Business information (Companies): Company name, description, business contact details, and details of published projects.
Usage data: Information about how you interact with the platform, access logs, and applications.

sections.title: 3. How We Use Information
paragraphs: We use your personal data exclusively to:
items: Enable the creation and management of your account on the platform.
Power the "matching" tool, connecting FWD Junior profiles with the technical requirements of the projects published by Companies.
Enable initial communication and applications to projects.
Send important notifications about the status of your projects, platform updates, or changes to our policies.
Improve the performance, security, and user experience of the marketplace.

sections.title: 4. Sharing and Disclosure of Data
paragraphs: The marketplace's core premise is to connect talent with opportunities. Therefore:
items: For FWD Juniors: When you apply to a project or make your profile public, registered Companies can see your name, skills, project history, and portfolio.
For Companies: Your company's general information and the details of published projects will be visible to registered Juniors.
sections.note: Commitment: Fundación Forward Costa Rica does not sell, rent, or trade your personal information with third parties outside the FWD Talent ecosystem under any circumstances.

sections.title: 5. Data Retention
paragraphs: We will retain your personal information while your account remains active or as needed to provide you with the platform's services. If you decide to delete your account, your personal data will be deleted or anonymized from our systems, except for data we must retain due to legal obligations or for dispute resolution.

sections.title: 6. Information Security
paragraphs: We implement technical and organizational security measures to protect your information against unauthorized access, loss, or alteration. This includes the use of encryption for passwords and secure communications. However, no system on the internet is 100% secure, so we urge you to use strong passwords and keep your credentials confidential.

sections.title: 7. Your Rights
paragraphs: You have the right to access, rectify, update, or request the deletion of your personal information at any time. You can manage most of your data directly from the "Profile" section on the platform. If you wish to exercise any additional right or request the complete deletion of your account, you can contact us.

sections.title: 8. Cookies and Similar Technologies
paragraphs: We use essential cookies to keep your session active and ensure safe browsing. We may also use analytics cookies on an anonymized basis to understand how the platform is used and improve our services. You can configure your browser to reject cookies, although this may affect how the site works.

sections.title: 9. Third-Party Services and AI
paragraphs: For the platform's operation and compatibility analysis (matching), we use third-party APIs (such as AI services to process skill matches). The data sent to these services is limited to strictly necessary information and is processed under strict confidentiality and privacy agreements.

sections.title: 10. Changes to This Policy
paragraphs: We reserve the right to update this Privacy Policy periodically to reflect changes in our practices or due to legal requirements. We will notify you of significant updates through a notice on the platform or by email.

sections.title: 11. Contact
paragraphs: If you have questions, queries, or concerns regarding the handling of your personal data or this Privacy Policy, please do not hesitate to contact the technical support team at Fundación Forward Costa Rica.

cosmos_profesional.title: From idea to reality
cosmos_profesional.description: Two roles, one shared path: from concept to real project on FWD Talent.
cosmos_profesional.cta_question: Ready for your first real project?

0.title: Create your account
0.desc: Sign up as an FWD graduate, complete your profile, and start exploring available projects.

1.title: Create your account
1.desc: Sign up as a company, describe your organization, and the kind of talent you need.

2.title: Publish the project
2.desc: Define the scope, required stack, and budget. The FWD team reviews and activates the project.

3.title: Submit your proposal
3.desc: Choose the project that best fits your skills and write your cover letter.

4.title: Receive proposals
4.desc: Review applications, request adjustments if needed, and choose the ideal graduate for your project.

5.title: Refine your proposal
5.desc: If the company requests changes, polish your proposal and demonstrate your ability to iterate.

6.title: Project awarded
6.desc: The project is awarded: the graduate gains real experience and the company receives the finished work.

marketplace_preview.title: Real projects. Not simulations
marketplace_preview.description: Companies post concrete projects with a defined stack, clear budget, and real scope. You pick what fits your skills, send your proposal, and build your first professional portfolio.

0.title: Landing page for a wellness startup
0.desc: Design and build a responsive landing page with an animated hero section and a lead-capture form.

1.title: REST API for a delivery app
1.desc: Build order, user, and notification endpoints for the MVP of a home-delivery application.

2.title: Sales metrics dashboard
2.desc: Control panel with daily sales charts, active users, and real-time conversion rate tracking.

diferenciadores.title: We are not Upwork
diferenciadores.description: We built a space for junior talent in Costa Rica to prove their worth. Every detail of the process is designed so both sides win.

0.title: Validated projects
0.desc: Every listing goes through an FWD team review before appearing in the marketplace. No noise — only real opportunities.

1.title: Verified talent
1.desc: FWD graduates only, with proven skills and a real portfolio. Zero empty profiles.

2.title: Guided process
2.desc: Support at every stage: from application to final delivery. You never navigate alone.

3.title: Direct contact
3.desc: No middlemen between graduate and company. Direct contact from the very first project.

0.q: Do I need work experience to apply?
0.a: No. FWD Talent is designed for graduates without formal experience. What matters is what you learned in the program and what you can demonstrate with your portfolio.

1.q: How does the company pay me?
1.a: Payment is coordinated directly between you and the company. FWD facilitates the contact and the process, but does not process payments. You can agree on bank transfer, PayPal, or other methods with each company.

2.q: Can I apply to several projects at the same time?
2.a: You can explore as many projects as you like, but you can only have one active application at a time. We recommend personalizing your cover letter to increase your chances.

3.q: How much does it cost to post a project as a company?
3.a: Access is free during the beta phase. Pricing plans based on posting volume are coming soon.

4.q: How do I know the graduate has the skills I need?
4.a: Each profile shows completed FWD projects, the stack they've mastered, and their program evaluation. You can review their portfolio before awarding the project.

5.q: How long does it take for my listing to be reviewed?
5.a: The FWD team reviews each listing within 48 business hours. You receive a notification when the project goes live in the marketplace.

6.q: What happens if I'm not satisfied with the delivered work?
6.a: The process includes a revision round before closing. You can request corrections through the platform. The FWD team can mediate if needed.

7.q: In which countries is FWD Talent available?
7.a: We currently operate in Costa Rica. Expansion to other Central American and LATAM countries is on the roadmap for the second half of the year.
